name: blst_meta_alloc
prose: Precondition: scan points to the root of the radix subtree (in the skip-linked array layout) whose first block is cursor rounded down to a multiple of radix*BLIST_RADIX and whose child radix is radix/BLIST_RADIX; radix is 1 or a positive power of BLIST_RADIX; cursor lies inside that extent; *count >= 1 and maxcount >= *count; the caller serializes access to the whole blist (the function takes no lock). Postcondition: if radix == 1 the result is exactly that of blst_leaf_alloc on this leaf. Otherwise the children whose bit is set at or after the cursor's digit are tried in increasing order, a child only if *count <= its bm_bighint, by a recursive call. If a recursive call returns a block r, r is returned at once, *count has been set by the callee to the number of blocks actually allocated (at least the requested *count and at most maxcount; the run may continue into following leaves), the allocated bits are cleared in leaf bitmaps and in the meta nodes along the way, and this node's bit for the tried child is cleared if that child's bitmap became zero. Otherwise the function returns SWAPBLK_NONE, *count is unchanged, no block was allocated and no bitmap bit changed; only bm_bighint fields may have been lowered: none of this node's own bighint is touched if no bit at or after the cursor's digit is set (early return); otherwise, after all candidate children failed, this node's bm_bighint is set to *count - 1 only if cursor was the first block of this node's extent and not (the last examined child was digit BLIST_RADIX-1 and its bm_bighint, after the recursive attempt, equals BLIST_MAX_ALLOC); descendants' bighints may also have been lowered by the recursive calls.
note: Rewritten from the code: early mask==0 return leaves bighint untouched; the BLIST_MAX_ALLOC exception tests the last examined child after recursion; success sets *count to the allocated size; no lock inside.

name: right_to_index
prose: Precondition: none; the index field idx = (right >> 57) & 0x1F is always in 0..31, so the internal assertion idx < 32 (the size of bit2idx) cannot fail for any 64-bit right. Postcondition: returns 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 when idx equals 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 respectively, and returns -1 for every other idx value (including 0 and all values with two or more bits set); it reads only a constant table, allocates nothing and takes no locks.
note: Scalar function: contract states the full table lookup on idx = (right >> 57) & 31 (CAPIDXBIT); requires true because the assertion cannot fail.

name: bioq_disksort
prose: Precondition: head points to an initialized bio_queue_head whose queue entries are valid and whose insert_point is either NULL or an element of the queue, bp points to a valid bio that is not on any queue, and the caller holds the lock that protects head (the function takes none). Postcondition: bp is linked into head->queue and head owns it until it is removed; the function returns nothing and never fails. Tail insertion (bioq_insert_tail) is used if BIO_ORDERED is set in bp->bio_flags, or if bp->bio_cmd is none of BIO_READ, BIO_WRITE and BIO_DELETE, or if bioq_batchsize > 0 and head->batched > bioq_batchsize: bp becomes the last element, head->total is incremented, head->batched is reset to 0, head->insert_point becomes bp and head->last_offset becomes bp->bio_offset. Otherwise (sorted insertion) bp is inserted after the last element, searching from the successor of head->insert_point (or from the first element if insert_point is NULL), that satisfies key(bp) >= key(cur) consecutively, where key(x) = (uoff_t)(x->bio_offset - head->last_offset); it is inserted at the head of the queue if insert_point is NULL and no such element precedes it; head->total and head->batched are each incremented by one and head->insert_point and head->last_offset are unchanged.
note: Fixed: batched is reset to 0 (not incremented) on every tail insertion, insert_point/last_offset updated; sorted path keeps them. The record slice 252-299 starts after the function name line (247), so the mechanical name check cannot pass for this record: slice boundary problem.
